t: Early Afro--South Asian Contacts May Shed Light on the Origins of Dravidian Languages
x: This paper reopens the Dravidian question from the perspective of early Afro–South Asian exchange. Archaeobotanical evidence, especially the third-millennium BCE movement of African domesticates such as pearl millet into South Asia, points to sustained interaction across the Arabian Sea. Together with selected comparative-linguistic observations, this evidence invites a broader reconstruction of Dravidian prehistory within an Afro–Arabian–South Asian interaction sphere. The paper argues that this transregional setting offers a productive new perspective on the cultural and linguistic background of the early Dravidian world.
